stories.title: Iran strikes ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in Hormuz
stories.lead: Three sources confirmed to Reuters an attack claimed on Tuesday by the Revolutionary Guards; smoke was visible but damage was not assessed.
stories.body: Shipping and maritime security sources expect a limited impact on commercial traffic, as other navigation systems exist. Gulf oil exports recovered to more than 80% of pre-war levels in September and October, helped by US military escorts, higher Saudi exports via Yanbu and ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar and Fujairah.
stories.why: Iran is now hitting infrastructure on neutral territory while the market prices peace, a reminder that Hormuz flows depend on workarounds that can be disrupted.

stories.title: Oil drops 1.6% on diplomacy hopes over Iran and Ukraine
stories.lead: Brent fell to $91.29 (-$1.47) and WTI to $85.29 (-1.43%) in Asian trade, after gaining 1.4% on Wednesday.
stories.body: A report pointed to further US-Iran diplomacy, while Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed a major prisoner exchange in Abu Dhabi without progress on territory. Higher OPEC+ output in October and a 9 million barrel API crude build added to oversupply worries; EIA data is due on Thursday, delayed by Veterans Day.
stories.why: The risk premium built on Wednesday vanished overnight, showing how fast headlines now swing crude around $90.

stories.title: Nvidia board reportedly prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang
stories.lead: Nvidia fell more than 8% after hours to $159.51, having lost over $450 billion in market value since the probe was announced on November 8.
stories.body: The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was meeting on Wednesday evening to decide on Huang's future after an internal investigation into his conduct; no official decision has been announced. Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.97% and Korea's Kospi fell 1.26%, dragged by Nvidia suppliers Samsung and SK Hynix.
stories.why: Nvidia is the largest weight in tech indices and the bellwether of AI chip demand, which drives power and copper demand from data centers; results are due on November 17.

stories.title: Gold slips below $4,000 as a 50 bp Fed hike enters the debate
stories.lead: Spot gold fell 0.4% to $3,973 an ounce and silver 0.6% to $51.36, with the dollar index at 102.98.
stories.body: A 25 bp Fed hike in December is fully priced and some investors now consider 50 bp, after Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called October inflation borderline disturbing. The US 2-year yield jumped 18 bp on Tuesday and the 10-year trades near 5%.
stories.why: Rising real rates weigh on non-yielding metals, and the Fed path now hinges on whether the energy shock spreads to wider prices.

stories.title: First Russian diesel cargo for the US idles off the East Coast
stories.lead: The White House plan allows 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel now, 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes after that; US diesel costs $6.13 a gallon, up 63% since February.
stories.body: Importers hesitate because of legal liability, bank reluctance to finance the deals and the need to blend the fuel to meet NYMEX heating oil specifications, while senators from both parties ask for the waiver to be rescinded. In Europe, northwest gasoline refining margins fell by more than $28 to $8.38 a barrel.
stories.why: Sanctions, financing and product specs can strand a cargo even when policy allows it, which keeps distillate cracks decoupled from crude.

stories.title: Ukrainian strikes knock out about 30% of Russia's refining capacity
stories.lead: Nine of Russia's 35 major refineries were disrupted in a week, about 2.2 mb/d of nameplate capacity out of roughly 6.8 mb/d.
stories.body: Industry estimates put the real loss of crude runs at up to 200,000 tonnes a day, around 1.5 mb/d, after refineries had partly recovered to about 5 mb/d at the end of October. The drone campaign has been running since late October and targets processing rather than crude exports.
stories.why: Less Russian refining means more crude available for export and fewer barrels of diesel, so product cracks and spreads can move independently of Brent.

stories.title: Oil edges back toward $92 as Iran deal hopes fade
stories.lead: Brent trades around $91.9 to $92.1 (+0.4 to 0.6%) and WTI near $86.4 after dipping below $90 on Tuesday.
stories.body: Up to 37 vessels were attacked near Hormuz in October, a record, and the IMO counts 130 since the war began; LSEG notes that higher flows would still depend on mine clearance, insurance and shipowners. On the supply side, OPEC output rose to 22.87 mb/d in October, about 90% of February levels, and the API reported a 9.0 million barrel build in US crude stocks.
stories.why: The paper market prices diplomacy while logistics remain the real bottleneck; official EIA stocks on Thursday and the IEA report on Friday are the next checks.

stories.title: Orlen cancels a long-term Qatar LNG contract; TTF rises 2.7%
stories.lead: Poland's Orlen is the first QatarEnergy customer to cancel a long-term deal, a 1 Mt per year contract signed in 2009 and running to 2034.
stories.body: QatarEnergy has been under force majeure since spring 2026, extended at the end of October to year-end. Qatari LNG exports fell to about 2.7 Mt in October from close to 6.2 Mt in February, even as LNG transits through Hormuz rose to 31. European gas climbed to about EUR87/MWh, with EU storage below 73% against a five-year average of 89%.
stories.why: A prolonged force majeure starts to break long-term contracts, pushing volumes toward the spot market and trader portfolios.

stories.title: Siemens Energy posts a record year but guides 2027 profit below consensus
stories.lead: Fourth-quarter revenue hit a record EUR12.83bn and the backlog EUR164bn, but 2027 net income guidance of about EUR5bn is roughly 10% below the EUR5.5bn consensus.
stories.body: Full-year 2026 net income rose to EUR4.13bn from EUR1.69bn, with a proposed dividend of EUR2.30. Quarterly orders of EUR14.82bn missed the EUR15.47bn expected. Gas turbines and grid equipment for data centers drive growth, with Gas Services revenue seen up 24 to 26% in 2027 and a 20 to 22% margin targeted for 2030.
stories.why: Data center power demand keeps turning into firm orders for gas turbines and grid equipment, a structural support for gas burn and copper-intensive grids.

stories.title: Wall Street slips after hot CPI; futures and Asia rebound on chips
stories.lead: On Tuesday the S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Nasdaq 0.74%, with Nvidia down 5.5%; this morning Nasdaq 100 futures are up 1.4% and the Kospi 2.6%.
stories.body: October CPI rose 0.4% month on month, above expectations. Nvidia's market value fell to about $4.07tn, its lowest since late March, amid the Jensen Huang affair. TSMC gained 2.2% after its board approved up to $1bn of investments in Anthropic and OpenAI, and the Nikkei rose 1.31%. The US bond market is closed today for Veterans Day.
stories.why: The chip supply chain, not Nvidia, is leading the rebound ahead of Nvidia's results on 17 November, a key test for AI-driven demand for chips, power and metals.

stories.body: Donald Trump said a new strike on Iran was unnecessary "at this stage", Qatar called for restraint and tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is picking up, to the point that Middle East producers are cutting prices to find buyers. Physical Gulf crude tells a different story: Abu Dhabi's Murban rose 3.4% to $99.17, about $7 above Brent, and attacks on ships near the strait continue.
stories.lead: Brent closed at $92.57 on Monday (-5.85%) and slipped again to about $91.3 to $92.3 this morning; WTI trades near $86 to $87.
stories.title: Oil: Brent at its lowest since 31 August as Hormuz flows resume
stories.why: The gap between paper and physical Gulf crude widened from about $1.70 to about $7 in a day. That spread is where physical traders make or lose money, and the EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook out today gives the official US read.

stories.body: Exports of integrated circuits more than doubled (+137.1%) to $39.59bn on AI-related demand. The cumulative surplus since January passes $1,040bn.
stories.lead: Exports rose 35.2% year on year (about $412bn) and imports 41.6% (about $307bn), both well above forecasts; the surplus narrowed to $105.3bn.
stories.title: China: imports jump 41.6% in October, trade surplus at its lowest since April
stories.why: Imports this strong support commodity demand at a time when physical copper is already tight in China. The product detail (crude, copper) comes with the full customs data.

stories.body: Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee has warned that the data-centre build-out looks like old-fashioned demand overheating. Markets priced about an 81% chance of a Fed hike on 9 December (CME FedWatch, cited by Reuters).
stories.lead: Core is expected at +0.2% after +0.6% headline and +0.3% core in September; no year-on-year rate will be published because October 2025 data are missing after the shutdown.
stories.title: US October CPI due at 14:30 Paris time: +0.3% m/m expected
stories.why: It is the last inflation print before the Fed meeting; a reading above 0.3% would reinforce the curve flattening seen since Friday's jobs report.

stories.body: This morning Korea's Kospi rose 4% to 5%, enough to trigger the brake on programme orders, the Nikkei 2.89% (SoftBank +13.4%, Tokyo Electron +4.7%) and SK Hynix 5.2%; S&P 500 futures are up 0.16%.
stories.lead: The S&P 500 gained 2.35%, the Nasdaq Composite 2.74% and the Dow 1,104 points (+2.2%) on Monday, while Nvidia fell about 4% on its board's inquiry into Jensen Huang.
stories.title: Wall Street posts its best day since 8 April; Asia follows on chipmakers
stories.why: After last week's AI sell-off, the rebound is led by equipment and memory makers rather than Nvidia, eight days before Nvidia's results on 17 November.

stories.body: Janus Henderson launched an active China equity ETF and Defiance the first equal-weight UCITS ETF on the Magnificent Seven. J.P. Morgan AM named Eve-Marie Bussière, from DWS, head of ETF distribution for France and Monaco.
stories.lead: Fidelity International launched an Equity Enhanced Yield range and now has more than thirty active ETFs; Man Group launched two (trend following and infrastructure).
stories.title: Active ETFs in Europe: Fidelity passes thirty products, Man Group launches its first UCITS active ETFs
stories.why: Active ETFs change the market maker's job: less transparent baskets and harder hedging.

note: Veille 2026-11-09, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: Brent slips to $96.45 after Trump, but physical Gulf crude rises
stories.lead: Brent fell 1.9% after a weekly drop of more than 16%, the steepest since 2020; WTI trades near $90.5 to $91.3.
stories.body: Donald Trump called a new strike on Iran very unlikely while talks progress. Abu Dhabi's Murban, a physical Gulf grade, rose 3.4% to $99.17, about $1.70 above Brent: a tanker was hit again in the Strait of Hormuz on 8 November and IMF PortWatch counted a single transit on 1 November against 85 a day before the crisis. JPMorgan still sees a global surplus of 1.4 mb/d in October.
stories.why: The gap between a paper market pricing peace and a still tight physical market is exactly what traders arbitrage.

stories.title: Nvidia board opens an inquiry into Jensen Huang, shares about -6% in early trading
stories.lead: Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 1% and S&P 500 futures 0.15%.
stories.body: On 8 November Jensen Huang acknowledged a relationship with a woman US agencies describe as a Chinese spy; a committee of independent directors is investigating and says it has no reason to believe secrets leaked. Friday had brought a rebound (Nasdaq +1.09%, S&P 500 +0.31%), and Taiwan's market rose 4.94% on Monday.
stories.why: A governance risk on the largest S&P 500 company, a week before its results on 17 November 2026.

stories.title: Copper: record physical squeeze in China, Trafigura buys at rising premiums
stories.lead: Shanghai's spot premium hit a record 2,615 yuan ($392) a tonne after tripling in two weeks; import premiums rose more than 40% to $195 to $210.
stories.body: The spread between the first two SHFE contracts topped 1,200 yuan, unseen since 2005, and deliverable stocks (33,848 t) cover less than a day of Chinese demand. Smelters lack concentrate and scrap, copper and cobalt trucks were seized in the DR Congo, and metal stayed in the United States on tariff fears. Trafigura has been asking producers and traders for November and December cargoes (Bloomberg).
stories.why: A concrete case of backwardation and physical premium on a key energy transition metal.

stories.title: Credit Agricole proposes to merge its Italian arm with Banco BPM
stories.lead: Friendly offer with a 20% premium for Banco BPM shareholders and a €1 billion special dividend.
stories.body: Credit Agricole would go from 29.6% to about 45% of a new group, Italy's third largest bank, listed in Milan. The deal needs a Banco BPM shareholder vote under the whitewash procedure, plus approval from the ECB and the Italian government; completion is targeted for the second half of 2027. UniCredit rose 4.7% the same morning on a record quarterly profit of €3.3 billion.
stories.why: European bank consolidation continues, with French and Italian lenders at the center.

stories.title: US October CPI due tomorrow: +0.2% to +0.3% month on month expected
stories.lead: FactSet expects +0.24% after +0.6% in September; core is seen near +0.2%.
stories.body: The BLS will not publish a year-on-year rate, for lack of October 2025 data after the shutdown. The probability of a Fed hike on 9 December 2026 is about 81% (CME FedWatch, via Reuters). In China, October producer prices rose 5.7% from a year earlier, the highest since June 2022, while consumer prices slowed to +0.7%.
stories.why: The last inflation print before the Fed, which will shape the flattening of the yield curve.

note: Veille 2026-11-06, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: AI stocks crash: S&P 500 -4.4%, Nasdaq -5.5%, chip index -12.2%
stories.lead: Worst S&P 500 session since April 2025; the Nasdaq Composite is 11.9% below its October record, in correction territory.
stories.body: Nvidia fell 9.3% and AMD 17.3%, while AppLovin jumped 31% on results. Investors fear a freeze on data centers after the Democratic wave, with about forty local measures to slow their construction and a call for a national moratorium, plus doubts on AI returns and higher borrowing costs. Money moved into Treasuries: the 10-year yield fell to 4.84% from 4.90%.
stories.why: A textbook flight to quality: equities down, long rates down, with the AI supply chain at the center.

stories.title: Asia follows: Nikkei about -5.9%, Kospi halted, Taiex -4.5%
stories.lead: The Kospi touched -8.8% intraday and lost about 11.7% over the week; TSMC fell as much as 8.5% in Taipei.
stories.body: SK Hynix lost about 10% and Samsung about 8%; Kioxia, SoftBank and Advantest also dropped sharply. China held up better (Hang Seng -0.7%). Euro Stoxx 50 futures were down about 1% early on, and gold fell 1.1% to $4,044 an ounce.
stories.why: The markets most exposed to memory and chip equipment pay for US political risk.

stories.title: Brent rebounds to $98.29 as tankers burn near Hormuz
stories.lead: Brent +3.9% to $98.29 and WTI to $91.07 after Wednesday's crash.
stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers and a tug caught fire after using unauthorised routes in the Strait of Hormuz; UKMTO counts at least five incidents in the Gulf since Sunday, and US crude and product stocks are falling. Eurasia Group cut the odds of a deal with Iran to 10% from 20% and sees Brent at $110 to $125 if tensions escalate.
stories.why: The geopolitical premium rebuilds as soon as maritime incidents resume, with freight, insurance and the Brent-WTI spread ($7.22) moving with it.

stories.title: US October jobs report today: about 60,000 to 65,000 jobs expected
stories.lead: Release at 14:30 Paris time, with unemployment seen at 4.2%.
stories.body: September added only 29,000 jobs and the monthly average since January 2025 is about 35,000. Signals this week were firm: ADP at 86,000, jobless claims at their lowest since July and JOLTS at 7.5 million. Markets price a 67% chance of a 25 basis point Fed hike on 9 December 2026 (CME FedWatch).
stories.why: A strong number would back a December hike while equities fall; a weak one would extend the rally in long bonds.

note: Veille 2026-11-05, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: Brent crashes 9.73% to $93.52, its biggest drop in months
stories.lead: Brent lost $10.08 on Wednesday to its lowest since 4 September 2026 and held near $93.6 on Thursday morning, against almost $118 on 30 October.
stories.body: The White House tied the Republican defeat in the midterms to the war with Iran, and the market started to price a deal. The physical market stays tight: US distillate stocks are 13% below their five-year average and Gulf exports fell to 17.1 mb/d in October from 18.9 mb/d in September, about three quarters of pre-war levels (Vortexa).
stories.why: Paper markets may have erased the Hormuz premium faster than physical flows justify.

stories.title: Bank of England expected to raise rates for the first time since August 2023
stories.lead: A Reuters poll sees a 7-2 vote to lift Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% at 13:00 Paris time.
stories.body: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, above expectations, on the energy shock from the war with Iran. Markets also price at least three more quarter-point hikes next year, which would take UK rates above US rates; some economists, such as PIMCO, expect only one, in February 2027.
stories.why: The gap between market pricing and economists is a live debate for sterling rates, and the oil slide may soften the Bank's message.

stories.title: Qualcomm beats on revenue but guides below, shares down about 6% after hours
stories.lead: Fourth-quarter revenue of $10.32 billion against $10.12 billion expected; adjusted EPS of $2.17.
stories.body: Handsets fell 26% from a year earlier while automotive and IoT rose 36%. The first-quarter outlook of $2.15 to $2.35 per share sits below the roughly $2.32 expected, because component costs, memory first, are rising; the $5 billion data center revenue goal for 2027 is unchanged.
stories.why: AI demand lifts memory prices and squeezes the margins of mobile chip makers: winners and losers from the same trend.

stories.title: Dow posts its best session since April 2025, Asia split on Thursday
stories.body: The end of election uncertainty and the fall in oil drove the rally. On Thursday the Nikkei fell about 1.5% on AI names, on fears that a Democratic Congress regulates data centers, while the broader Topix rose; gold traded near $4,135 an ounce.
stories.why: A clear rotation: cyclicals and banks up, AI down on political risk.

stories.title: ArcelorMittal posts a net loss on the Kryvyi Rih shutdown, adjusted profit rises
stories.lead: Third-quarter net loss of $391 million after $852 million of impairments and $293 million of exceptional charges tied to the Ukrainian site.
stories.body: Adjusted net income rose to $868 million from $683 million in the second quarter, and EBITDA of about $2.02 billion beat the $1.96 billion consensus (LSEG). Net debt reached $10.3 billion at end-September, swollen by $2.5 billion of working capital expected to unwind in the fourth quarter; the group sees double-digit growth in European flat steel shipments.
stories.why: Europe's steel demand is turning up while the war keeps weighing on Ukrainian iron ore and steel capacity.

note: Veille 2026-11-03, brief du matin (written on 10 Nov 2026 from the sourced brief)

stories.title: Oil rebounds about 1% after a reported US strike on Qeshm, a day after a 7.6% slide
stories.lead: Brent closed Monday at $104.77 (-7.63%) and WTI at $96.46 (-7.4%), then climbed back to about $106 and $96.9 on Tuesday morning.
stories.body: Monday's drop followed signs of diplomacy between Washington and Tehran. Overnight, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials, a US strike on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz, described as defensive and not confirmed by CENTCOM. JD Vance said he was optimistic about a negotiated settlement, and Donald Trump answered no when asked whether he would strike Iran after the elections.
stories.why: Diplomacy and limited strikes now move together, so the Hormuz risk premium can vanish or return within a single session.

stories.title: Reserve Bank of Australia lifts its cash rate to 4.85%, the highest since 2008
stories.lead: Fifth hike of 2026, from 4.60% to 4.85%, voted six to three.
stories.body: The central bank pointed to high inflation, the war in the Middle East and the rise in oil prices. Governor Michele Bullock left the door open to further hikes but hinted at a pause to assess the effect of the five moves; the three dissenters wanted to hold.
stories.why: A first clear case of a central bank tightening because of the oil shock, ahead of the Bank of England decision on Thursday.

stories.title: Wall Street ends lower despite oil, Apple slips after results
stories.lead: The S&P 500 lost 0.51% to 7,541.40, a third straight fall, and the Nasdaq 1.07%, while the Dow gained 0.41%.
stories.body: After the close, Apple reported quarterly revenue of $114.5 billion (+12%), including $57.6 billion from the iPhone (+17%), but fell about 3% after hours on a lower gross margin outlook tied to memory costs. Palantir, with revenue up 96% and a raised annual outlook, also slipped about 3%.
stories.why: Memory costs are becoming a common thread across the chip and hardware chain, a sign of how AI demand reprices inputs.
